title: Partnered starts grow without end, faster than any cluster reading
claim: Theorem 1: the partnered start of order n >= 3 (2n live points in partner pairs, blocks the non-partner pairs, open counts 2^(n-1)) keeps the partnered form at every stage, with N_0 = 2n, N_1 = 2^n, N_(t+1) = 2^(N_t/2) - N_(t-1); no offshoot, stall or close; runaway growth. Lemma 2: the next round has at least mc(G[W]) - |blocks| - lone groups for any set W of live points; a partnered set of order k >= 2 gives 2^k - |blocks|. Lemma 3: a partnered set of order k >= 2 with no outside common candidate gives a partnered set of order 2^(k-1) - |blocks| at the next stage. Corollary 4: no cluster reading with clusters of polynomially many members follows a partnered start.
standard_statement: Neumann-Lara's K(O_n) = O_(2^(n-1)) for the clique-graph operator, with the cliques held by blocks removed; injection of an induced subgraph's maximal cliques.
prior_work: Neumann-Lara 1978 (clique-divergent octahedra); Cedillo and Pizana 2021 (clique-convergence undecidable for automatic graphs); REDUCE-BLOCKS-20261119-001 (Lemma R); DOUBLE-IDENT-20261119-001 (cluster reading).
